newsitem.title: BELGIUM: D'IETEREN FIRST-HALF NET PROFITS UP 137 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: D'IETEREN FIRST-HALF NET PROFITS UP 137 PERCENT.

text.p: D'Ieteren NV, Belgium's largest car importer and distributor, on Tuesday posted first-half consolidated group net profits of 589 million francs, up 137 percent on last year's first six months.
Chairman, Roland D'Ieteren, said the results and current favourable trends should bring higher net profits for 1996.
"The improvement of the first semester should be kept, and probably lightly improved," he said.
Car imports earned after-tax profit of 686 million francs, and car rentals contributed 214 million francs, before goodwill write-offs of 311 million francs.
The company held an unchanged 19.7 percent share of new car sales in Belgium, and turnover rose to 29.052 billion francs from 26.171 billion in the first half of 1995.
D'Ieteren imports and distributes Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Seat and Skoda cars.
It also holds 77.1 percent of car rental firm Avis Europe, increased from 68 percent in February.
